disputes.reason: Classification of an error rate depends on context; error or failure rates are commonly used as KCIs or KRIs, so a standalone claim that it is a KCI (and the correction that it is a KPI) is arguable.

Vague and unanswerable without the source: 'directive controls are always part of control taxonomies' tests no syllabus fact, and the explanation (they are used but do not always appear in taxonomies) is not a teachable point.

Arguable as true: the testing method chosen (reperformance is the most rigorous) plainly influences how effective control testing is; the false label rests on a narrow reading of the three named factors.

Not clearly false: outsourcing risk analysis can include vendor financial/liquidity viability, so 'liquidity risk is not included' depends on an unstated list; the explanation calling it a balance-sheet risk is contestable.

Ambiguous and misattributed: there is no 'EBA Irish stress test'; the 2011 EBA test found no Irish bank failing, so the statement could be read as true, while the Irish (PCAR) test did reveal a capital need.
